A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, five figures, Table 1, and appendices are readable and can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 report original reasoning accuracy, repetition rates, and latency/throughput measurements. Appendix A.2 includes additional penalty-sweep results.

after.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix A.2 retain the work's original reasoning, repetition, and runtime experimental results.

M1.justification: Section 3 corrects the match-extension adjustment from log(1-(d-l+1)/(l*d))-1 to log(1+(d-l-1)/(l*d))-1. This changes the written scoring rule locally; the LZSS simulation and overall logit update remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GPQA and AIME reasoning tasks and the same runtime benchmark. Intentional repetition and multimodal applications are discussed in v4 without new evaluations.

E2.justification: Figures 2, 4, and 5 retain the same no-penalty, repetition-penalty, and frequency-penalty comparisons. Table 1 retains the same comparisons with and without LZ.

E3.justification: The models, generation settings, LZ hyperparameters, temperature/penalty sweeps, and runtime benchmark configuration remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 supplies detector details without establishing that the existing evaluation protocol changed.

E4.justification: The temperature and penalty-strength sweeps and the Cursor/Gemini repetition example are retained. The new intentional-repetition limitation is hypothetical; no additional ablation, robustness test, or case-study result is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy means and empirical standard deviations over five runs, with the same error-bar convention. Runtime medians are retained, and no new seed information or uncertainty procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 2 and appendix Figures 4–5 contain identical plotted results. Table 1 retains every latency, throughput, and slowdown value, including 0.55%, 0.14%, and 0.03% slowdowns. The revised illustrative penalty range belongs to the mathematical correction assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the algebraic identity underlying the match-extension branch and revises its dynamic-range derivation. v4 adds the conditions |w| >= |b|+2 and d >= l+2, changing the example's minimum adjustment from -5 to approximately -1. The broader theoretical framework is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract retains the claims of greedy decoding without capability loss or degenerate repetition and the inadequacy of standard penalties. The new conclusion restates these claims and the previously reported negligible runtime overhead.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands applicability and failure-condition discussion through explicit limitations: intentional repetitions may suffer, applications outside natural language may need different compressors, and hyperparameter complexity and implementation overhead require consideration. These qualifications were not developed as limitations in v3.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.3 provides the GPT-4o judge prompt, structured boolean output convention, and a minimum substring length of three for exact-repetition detection. These are newly documented details of the existing detector; hardware and benchmark implementation information are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to the GPT-5, Qwen3, and DeepSeek-R1 reports, Schmidhuber's intrinsic-motivation work, and Delétang et al. on compression. These modestly expand background connections while retaining the existing research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 expands the title, corrects wording, changes vocabulary notation to alphabet notation, and reorders definitions within Section 2.2. It also adds explanatory passages, limitations, a conclusion, and Appendix A.3; most existing exposition and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: All five figure images and the table structure are retained. Journal headers, page flow, figure placement, and captions change, including moving the frequency heatmap onto a separate appendix page and clarifying penalty names in captions.

improvement.justification: v4 improves mathematical consistency by correcting the match-extension formula and its range, makes the repetition detector more reproducible, and states concrete applicability limits. These provide focused gains in correctness and transparency while retaining the same empirical evidence.
